Adjusted assessment using Beige Book insights:
- Economic activity expanded from October to mid-November, consistent with “moderate” growth. Consumer spending and services were steady, while manufacturing was mixed.
- Labor markets remained tight, with firms reporting difficulty finding qualified workers; in some districts this constrained business growth, aligning with the FOMC’s “strong labor market” language.
- Price pressures were subdued and mixed: energy and steel prices were flat to down; some retailers reported an ability to raise prices, but overall inflation remained muted—consistent with inflation running below 2%.
- Banking conditions temper the outlook: weaker C&I loan demand (including at foreign banks serving middle‑market firms) and softer construction/land development loan demand, with some tightening attributed to the economic outlook and liquidity. This corroborates the FOMC’s note on weak business investment.

Net: The Beige Book broadly validates the modestly positive tone of the FOMC statement but, together with weaker loan demand and some tightening, warrants a touch more caution. sentiment score = 0.17
